name: crab-clean
short_description: A Rust-powered command-line tool that automates smart grouping and safe deletion to keep workspaces lean.
detailed_description: Built a high-performance system cleaning utility leveraging Rust's zero-cost abstractions for fast duplicate and unused file cleanup.
Designed a multi-threaded scanning architecture using Rayon, achieving 90% faster file hashing via optimized SHA-256 and parallel disk I/O.
Published and distributed via Crates.io with 926 active downloads.

case_study.summary: A Rust CLI that hunts duplicate files at native speed by parallelizing every step of the scan.
problem: Most disk-cleanup tools spin on a single thread and bottleneck on hashing.
Filename heuristics false-flag legitimate files as duplicates.
Workspace junk piles up faster than typical cleaners can chew through.
approach: Rayon's work-stealing pool parallelizes traversal, hashing, and grouping.
SHA-256 streams in 4 KB chunks so peak memory stays flat regardless of file size.
Files only collapse into a duplicate group on matching size AND full content hash — never on filename alone.
result: Cleared a 320 GB workspace in roughly eight minutes on an M2.
Around 90% faster than the single-threaded baseline.
Shipped to crates.io as crab-clean with 926 active downloads at time of writing.

name: solana-indexer
short_description: A lightweight, customizable SDK for indexing data from the Solana blockchain with automatic reorg handling.
detailed_description: Engineered a scalable data pipeline to efficiently index block, transaction, and account activity on Solana.
Built on tokio for asynchronous processing, allowing seamless backfilling and real-time updates via RPC polling, WebSockets, or Helius Webhooks.
Features a modular architecture with IDL-based type generation, providing a decoupled SDK for custom instruction decoding and type-safe event handling.

case_study.summary: A modular Rust SDK that turns raw Solana on-chain activity into typed, reorg-safe streams.
problem: Every team building on Solana rebuilds the same plumbing: RPC, WebSockets, reorg detection, decoding.
Most builds are brittle scripts that break the next time a program's IDL changes.
Backfilling and live streams are usually wired separately, then drift apart over time.
approach: Modelled as a typed pipeline: source → IDL-aware decode → swappable sink.
Three source modes share one decode path — RPC poll, WebSocket subscription, Helius webhook.
Tokio drives async work; reorg detection compares finalized slot windows and replays from the divergence.
result: Powers both ShadowLend and SolidKYC internally.
Backfills a million slots in under six minutes on a Helius free-tier endpoint.

name: ShadowLend
short_description: A privacy-preserving lending protocol on Solana protecting user balances from predatory liquidation using Arcium TEEs.
detailed_description: Designed a hybrid privacy architecture protecting user deposit and borrow balances using client-side encryption and Ed25519 signatures.
Developed Solana smart contracts in Anchor for secure asset custody, validating off-chain Arcium execution attestations.
Implemented risk calculation logic (Interest, Health Factor) directly inside Arcium MXEs (Trusted Execution Environments) to secure borrowing positions.

case_study.summary: Solana lending where borrow positions and balances stay private — confidential compute inside Arcium TEEs verifies risk without exposing user data.
problem: Public on-chain lending exposes every borrow position to liquidation bots.
Whales get front-run on liquidations; small users get harvested for fees on every health-factor swing.
Privacy isn't a luxury here — it's a fairness primitive.
approach: User balances are client-side encrypted before they ever touch the chain.
Risk math (interest, health factor) runs inside Arcium MXEs — Trusted Execution Environments that produce attestations.
The Anchor program holds the assets but only ever sees proofs that a position is healthy or eligible for liquidation.
result: Solvency still enforceable on-chain via TEE attestations rather than plaintext state.

name: CodeSync
short_description: Real-time collaborative coding environment with integrated whiteboard and AI chat.
detailed_description: Built real-time collaborative coding with whiteboard and AI chat using Gemini API
Optimized sync latency by 30% using Liveblocks and Convex reactive database
Implemented conflict-free resolution, reducing editing conflicts by 50%
Designed role-based permissions for room owners to manage user access

case_study.summary: Real-time collaborative coding with a shared whiteboard and an AI pair, all running over CRDTs.
problem: Screen-share tools let you watch but never edit together.
Generic doc collab tools have no terminal, no AI, no shared canvas.
None of them let two engineers actually pair-program with an AI in the room.
approach: Editor built on Liveblocks for sub-100ms CRDT edit sync.
Convex backs persistent room state, permissions, and chat.
Gemini is a first-class room participant — replies stream into chat, proposed edits land as suggested CRDT operations.
result: Sync latency improved ~30% over the polling prototype.
Editing conflicts dropped ~50% after the CRDT migration.

name: Hackverse
short_description: Scalable hackathon platform with secure RBAC and optimized database architecture.
detailed_description: Developed secure RBAC using Passport.js, NestJS guards, and decorators
Designed normalized PostgreSQL schema with Prisma ORM for efficient data storage
Built full-stack app with PostgreSQL, Next.js, and NestJS for scalability
Implemented Redux for consistent global state management

case_study.summary: A full-stack hackathon platform with normalized data, role-based access, and a scalable NestJS backend.
problem: Existing platforms trust either everyone or no one — no middle ground.
Multi-event organizations need fine-grained RBAC without modal hell.
Schemas usually end up denormalized and inconsistent across events.
approach: NestJS guards and decorators express permissions declaratively at the controller layer.
Passport.js for auth; Postgres + Prisma keep the schema normalized and enforced at the DB level.
Next.js + Redux for the shared state that crosses team and event boundaries.
result: Multi-event coordination working with role-based access.
Organizers, judges, and participants each get scoped views.

name: SolidKYC
short_description: Privacy-preserving on-chain KYC verification system using Solana and Zero-Knowledge Proofs.
detailed_description: Designed and implemented a decentralized KYC system where users prove identity validity without revealing personal data using Zero-Knowledge Proofs.
Built Solana smart contracts using Anchor to verify zk-SNARK proofs on-chain and manage verification state.
Integrated Circom and snarkjs to generate and verify cryptographic proofs for off-chain identity validation.
Implemented wallet-based authentication and transaction signing using Solana Wallet Adapter.
Developed a React-based frontend to handle proof generation, wallet interaction, and on-chain verification flow.
Ensured non-custodial identity ownership by allowing users to control credentials locally while only submitting proofs to the blockchain.

case_study.summary: On-chain KYC where the user proves age, residency, and document validity to a Solana program without ever revealing the underlying data.
problem: Centralized KYC providers hoard sensitive personal data — passports, IDs, addresses.
Most on-chain KYC builds copy the same model with extra steps.
The privacy story breaks the moment any single party can correlate raw inputs.
approach: Circom circuits generate Groth16 proofs over the predicates that matter: over-18, country-in-allowlist, doc-from-trusted-issuer.
Proofs verify on-chain in an Anchor program that maintains a registry of verified wallets.
Users hold credentials locally; only the proof ever leaves their device.
result: Wallet connect → local proof generation via snarkjs → on-chain verification tx.
Frontend never touches raw KYC data; the program only sees the proof, not the inputs.
